parties:
Nisha Rani Devi ------ Petitioner
vs
National Board of Revenue, People’s Republic of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 12. In the instant case the petitioner having admitted to have sold finished goods (electrical cables) which are subject to taxation, cannot be allowed to say that she is not liable to pay tax because the DCT did not make any assessment. In the case of Kadarnath Jute Mft Co. Ltd. Vs Commissioner of Income Tax (Central) Calcutta reported in (1971) 28 STC 672 (SC) it was held that the liability to payment of tax is independent of the assessment. Furthermore the amount paid in excess, if any, has to be claimed under the specific provision made in that behalf under section 27 of the Sales Tax Act which provides that an application for refund has to be made in the prescribed manner within 4(four) years of the end of the year in which the tax in respect of which the refund is claimed was paid. But in the instant case the application for refund as contained in Annexure-B was filed on 26-7-86 although the refund related to tax paid in respect of assessment years 1975-76 and 1976-77 i.e after an inordinate delay of 9 (nine) years. The claim of refund is thus barred by limitation and Sales Tax Act being a Special Act having provided for special period of limitation there is no scope for extension of time by any authority.
